A2.text:
Nigar and Elvin live in Baku near the Boulevard. Today is December 31st. It is a very special day. It is the new year, and it is also their wedding anniversary.

They wanted to celebrate in a fancy restaurant tonight. Elvin bought new clothes. Nigar helped to decorate their small living room with bright lights and a small tree.

At five o'clock, Nigar's phone suddenly rang. It was her older brother, Rashad.

“We are in Baku for the holiday!” Rashad said. “We want to see you.”

Nigar looked at Elvin. They had an expensive table at the restaurant. But Nigar really missed her family from Quba.

“Let's invite them here,” Elvin smiled. “We can stay home. We can have a party together.”

Nigar called the restaurant and canceled their table. Then, they walked to the supermarket and bought a lot of food. They cooked a big feast for the whole family.

At eight o'clock, Rashad arrived with his wife and three children. The flat was very noisy and happy. They ate roast chicken, rice, and sweet pakhlava.

At midnight, everybody went out to the balcony. They watched the beautiful fireworks over the Caspian Sea.

“This is the best anniversary,” Nigar said. Elvin held her hand and agreed. A quiet restaurant was nice, but a big family party was much better.

options: She is very happy they stayed home

B1.text:
Nigar and Elvin had big plans for December 31st. It was not just the holiday; it was their third wedding anniversary. They had booked a table at an expensive restaurant near the Boulevard. They wanted to dress up and ring in the new year with a quiet, romantic evening.

To get ready, Nigar spent the afternoon cleaning their flat. She loved to decorate the living room with fairy lights and candles to make it look special.

Just as Elvin was ironing his shirt, Nigar's phone rang. It was her older brother, Rashad.

“Surprise! We drove down from Quba,” Rashad said loudly. “We are in Baku for the night. Can we come over to say hello?”

Nigar covered the phone and looked at Elvin. She felt terrible. It was an important family tradition to spend the holiday together, but they had paid a deposit for the restaurant.

“Tell them to come,” Elvin said without hesitation. “We can cancel the table. A family gathering is more important.”

Nigar smiled brightly and invited her brother. Then, the couple hurried to the nearby supermarket. They bought fresh bread, salads, cheese, and a huge chocolate cake. Instead of a fancy dinner for two, they prepared a wonderful feast for seven people.

Rashad and his family arrived at eight o'clock, bringing homemade pakhlava and joyful chaos into the small flat. The children played games while the adults drank tea and talked for hours.

At midnight, they all squeezed onto the balcony to watch the fireworks light up the Caspian Sea.

The next morning, Nigar and Elvin woke up late. Nigar opened the fridge and laughed. “We have enough leftovers for a whole week,” she said.

“Good,” Elvin smiled. “That was the best anniversary ever.”

B2.text:
For Nigar and Elvin, the thirty-first of December was always a double celebration. Not only was the whole of Baku buzzing with holiday excitement, but it also marked their wedding anniversary. This year, they had decided to go all out. They booked a corner table at a luxurious rooftop restaurant near the Boulevard, planning to paint the town red and ring in the new year in style.

By late afternoon, the flat was filled with a quiet sense of festivity. Nigar had taken the time to decorate the living room with elegant silver garlands, simply because she loved the atmosphere. Elvin was just polishing his best shoes when Nigar's mobile buzzed with a video call. It was her older brother, Rashad, calling from his car.

“Guess where we are!” Rashad beamed, panning the camera to show the familiar streets of Ganjlik. “We drove down from Quba on a whim. We'd love to stop by and see you both, if you're free.”

Nigar muted the microphone, her face falling slightly as she looked at Elvin. Breaking their longstanding tradition of a romantic anniversary dinner felt disappointing, and they had already paid a non-refundable deposit.

“Tell them to come over,” Elvin said, instantly reading her expression. “We can cancel the restaurant. Honestly, the more the merrier.”

Relieved, Nigar eagerly invited them. The romantic evening was immediately replaced by a frantic mission. The couple rushed to the nearest supermarket, frantically filling their trolley with cold cuts, fresh salads, and a massive chocolate cake. By the time Rashad arrived with his wife and three energetic kids, the kitchen island had been transformed into a glorious feast.

The flat echoed with laughter and warm conversation. The impromptu gathering turned out to be far more entertaining than any stiff restaurant dinner could have been. At the stroke of midnight, the entire family crowded onto the narrow balcony, watching the spectacular fireworks reflect off the dark waters of the Caspian Sea.

Waking up on New Year's Day, Nigar opened the fridge to make breakfast and burst out laughing.

“Well,” she called out to Elvin, “I hope you like pakhlava and potato salad, because we have enough leftovers to last until February.”
